text:
acme_ops: Hey team — over the last hour our app's requests to Redwood are getting routed to EU edges (extra ~180ms) even though we set region=us-west. Any idea why?

jess_support: Sorry you're seeing that. Can you paste an example request header or a request ID so we can trace?

acme_ops: Here's a redacted request we captured: `GET /v1/generate`
Headers:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
Client-Region: us-west,
User-Agent: acme-service/2.1
```
Request ID (from our client): `rqt_8b3f1a`

jess_support: thx. Noted the trailing comma on `Client-Region` — that might be the culprit. Tagging @mike_runtime and @anya_sre to confirm routing behavior.

mike_runtime: Thanks. If the header value includes a trailing comma it won't match the normalized region list `us-west|us-east|eu-central` and our router falls back to the default region policy (which for that account is `eu-central`). That matches the symptom (cross-region routing -> latency).

anya_sre: I can confirm in the access logs we saw `client_region="us-west,"` for the request id `rqt_8b3f1a` and the router decision was `fallback->eu-central` with reason `region_unrecognized`.

routing-bot: route-decision: request=rqt_8b3f1a, incoming_region="us-west,", normalized_region=none, final_route=eu-central, reason=region_unrecognized

mike_runtime: Quick mitigation: we can add a transient rule in the routing layer to strip trailing punctuation from `Client-Region` headers for the account `acme-corp` while we roll a proper fix. That will map `us-west,` -> `us-west`.

ricardo_cs: @acme_ops we can schedule a short maintenance window for the workaround if you want us to apply it now. ETA ~15 mins for the rule to propagate. Do you have high-volume traffic right now?

acme_ops: We're ramping traffic but can accept a brief window. Please proceed, and we'd appreciate a root-cause fix so our SDK doesn't keep doing this.

mike_runtime: Action items: 1) temporary routing rule to normalize region headers for acme-corp (SRE to apply). 2) runtime patch to strip non-alphanum and trailing punctuation from region header parsing (will open PR). 3) SDK owners to add defensive trimming and validation.

anya_sre: Applying transient rule now. Will post when propagation completes.

routing-bot: route-change: rule=strip-trailing-punct-for-account-acme-corp, status=applied, change_id=RC-4521

anya_sre: Propagation looks good. Can you re-run the failing request and share new request id?

acme_ops: Re-ran -> new request id `rqt_8b3f1b`. Header now still shows `Client-Region: us-west,` from our end (we haven't shipped SDK patch), but I think router should normalize.

routing-bot: route-decision: request=rqt_8b3f1b, incoming_region="us-west,", normalized_region=us-west, final_route=us-west, reason=transient_rule_match

acme_ops: Confirmed — now routed to us-west and latency back to expected. Thanks!

mike_runtime: I'll open the runtime PR to make header parsing resilient across all accounts. Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/+/PR-789 (summary: strip leading/trailing non-alphanumeric, collapse whitespace, lowercase).

jess_support: For immediate guidance to ACME's engineers: recommend trimming trailing punctuation from region header client-side e.g. `regionHeader = regionHeader.trim().replace(/[.,;]+$/,'')` and add a validation check that region is in allowed list.

ricardo_cs: I'll follow up with acme onboarding to make sure their SDK teams get the fix.

mike_runtime: Postmortem plan: 1) deploy runtime parser fix (next release, low-risk). 2) add unit tests around weird header values. 3) add a router metric for `region_unrecognized` so we can spike-alert on account-level misroutes.

acme_ops: Really appreciate the quick help. One ask: can you include the routing-bot logs in the ticket so we can map our client-side logs to your decisions?

jess_support: Will include the bot traces and example logs in the support ticket. Closing the thread once runtime PR is merged and we confirm no regressions. :thumbsup:

mike_runtime: FYI, patch landed in staging branch, CI green. Will schedule prod rollout after one more smoke test.

anya_sre: Prod rollout complete. Monitoring looks stable.

acme_ops: All good from our side. Thanks again everyone! :tada:
